channel.title: Aditya Firmansyah — Field Notes
channel.description: Practitioner notes on software engineering, AI agents, and self-hosting. English and Bahasa Indonesia.

item.title: Why next/font/google Broke Our CI: Self-Hosting 13 Font Subsets for Zero-Network Builds
item.description: Our master CI died twice in twelve hours inside next/font/google, on commits that carried identical font code. Here is how Dagango.com vendors 13 font subsets on disk and makes next build fetch nothing.

item.title: The SQLAlchemy Session Poisoning Trap in Bulk CSV Import
item.description: One failed row in a bulk import can poison a shared SQLAlchemy session and kill the next 497. Here is the real session-lifecycle fix, with numbers from PostgreSQL 18.6.

item.title: Reproducing the .git Hook Attack: git status Runs an Attacker's Command
item.description: Frank Wiles got a fake project inquiry, a Dropbox folder of specs, and a hidden .git with a post-checkout hook. I reproduced both vectors on git 2.53.0, and the popular fix is overridable.

item.title: My 17 Agents Remember With 1,069 Markdown Skills, Not Vectors
item.description: A memory plugin attaches the five most similar snippets to every prompt. I run 17 agents, and their durable knowledge is 1,069 Markdown skill files plus a memory file I keep under a kilobyte.

item.title: A Database Per Agent Costs More Than a File
item.description: Supabase says agents should be able to create a database as cheaply as a file. I already run one database per agent on a mini-PC, so I counted. The create is free; everything after it is the bill.

item.title: You Said No MCP: The Tool-Loadout Tradeoff Nobody Tests
item.description: Pi spent a year saying it would never speak MCP, then shipped it in the core. The reason was not that MCP got better. The sandbox underneath it did.

item.title: Git 3.0's SHA-256 Default Is a Primary-Key Migration
item.description: I created a SHA-256 repository with the git I already have. Two of three daily operations failed outright, and the third is documented to die on older clients. The hash is not the migration; the key is.

item.title: 18 Gateways to 1: The Fix That Isn't in Git
item.description: Eighteen gateway daemons became one in under three minutes. The dashboard watching them broke, then got fixed with 270 uncommitted lines. A clean checkout puts production back to reporting 16 of 17 profiles down.

item.title: Two Kinds of Decision, and No Way to Prove the Model Did Not Change
item.description: A reasoning classifier and a drift benchmark landed a day apart. Together they say which decisions deserve thinking, and why your own latency numbers cannot prove the model changed.

item.title: Egress Is the Boundary: What 700 Escaped Agents Taught About Containment
item.description: A forensic report on 700 escaped agents reads better as a containment checklist than an incident recap. Here is what it changed about how I run my own fleet.

item.title: Why We Built Isolated Subdomains Instead of a Public Store Directory
item.description: A public /stores directory would have made Dagango.com behave like a marketplace. We shipped per-tenant host routing and metadata instead, and the crawl-budget argument is what settled it.

item.title: Why Your Postgres LIKE Query Silently Seq Scans (And the One-Line Fix)
item.description: On a default en_US.UTF-8 Postgres, a UNIQUE (tenant_id, slug) index cannot serve LIKE 'prefix%' queries. Here are the benchmark numbers at 20,000 rows and the varchar_pattern_ops index that fixes it.

item.title: Your Agent's Config Silently Failed: The Canary Test That Catches It
item.description: Claude Code shipped AGENTS.md support gated behind a remote flag, so telemetry-off users got silent failures. Here's the five-second test that catches this class of bug in any agent setup.

item.title: Self-Hosting Behind CGNAT: A WireGuard Bridge That Actually Works
item.description: Port forwarding stopped working and it wasn't your router's fault. Here's the outbound WireGuard tunnel pattern that gets a homelab back on the public internet under CGNAT.

item.title: AI Agents Flooded Our PR Queue: Fixing CI Before It Breaks
item.description: Coding agents made writing PRs nearly free, which means your pipeline is now the bottleneck. Here's what Linear's CI rework maps to on a small-team budget.

item.title: Why I Self-Host Everything on a Mini PC
item.description: A Celeron box with 14GB RAM in the corner of my room runs my stores, my agents, and this blog. Here is the math on why cloud bills stopped making sense.
